meta.title: Word Parts in Our Club Week

paragraphs: Word Parts in Our Club Week, posted by Lily. Teacher Kim gave us a word game at the club hour. "Many English words have parts," she said. "A small part at the start is a prefix, and a small part at the end is a suffix." The Explorers looked for word parts at school and at the science museum. This post shows what we found. I wrote every new word in a table in my notebook.

The prefix "un" means "not". If you add "un" to "happy", you get "unhappy". Leo's bookshelf was untidy, because the books were on the floor. Leo put the books back, and then the bookshelf was tidy. At the museum, there was a chemistry show. Guide Ann mixed two liquids, and the mix turned blue. She said, "Never touch unsafe things."

The prefix "re" means "again". If you write a word again, you "rewrite" it. I always rewrite my blog posts, and Teacher Kim reads them. Guide Ann asked us to reuse our water bottles. In the technology room, a robot refilled our cups with water. It was a simple machine, but it worked well. Everybody wanted a second cup.

The suffix "er" can mean "a person who does something". A teacher teaches, a painter paints, and a runner runs. Mia likes the word "photographer", because it names a person with a camera. Be careful, because not every word with "er" names a person. "Supper" is a meal, so it is not a person who does something. Even Leo knew that, and he laughed.

The suffix "less" means "without". A careless person does not take care, and a useless thing has no use. The suffix "ful" means "with" or "full of". A helpful guide gives help, and a colorful poster has many colors. Leo made a new word, "bookless", and it means "without a book". May was mad about her useless pen, but Mia gave her a new one.

The suffix "ly" often makes an adverb, for example "quickly", "slowly", and "carefully". If you walk with care, you walk carefully. Teacher Kim says that a word part helps you guess a new word. Now we find word parts everywhere. Next week, we want to look for more word parts in the town library. Which word parts do you know? Write a new word in a message!
